data.cultural_impact: Myrian, as the neuter form of the Greek goddess name Myrrhine, could potentially evoke maritime associations. This is reminiscent of the biblical Magi, who arrived by ship to present gifts to the newborn Jesus. Myrrh was one of these gifts, contributing to the nautical theme.
data.spiritual_significance: Myrrh is described in the Bible as a precious and fragrant substance that was used to anoint the body of Jesus. In Christian tradition, myrrh symbolizes sorrow, suffering, and the sweetness of sacrifice. Since Myrian is the neuter form of Myrrhine, it may be seen as a reminder of the sacrifice Jesus made for humanity and the preciousness of the Christian faith.
